newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies retrial in Florida tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies retrial in Florida tobacco case.

text.p: A judge has refused a request by Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp. to overturn a precedent-setting jury award of $750,000 to a smoker with lung cancer.
Circuit Judge Brian Davis denied the tobacco company's motion in a one-page ruling issued on Wednesday and made public in the clerk of court's office on Friday.
The ruling means that Brown & Williamson can now appeal the Aug. 9 jury award to a higher court.
The company had asked Davis to overturn the jury ruling, claiming that the judge erred in admitting testimony about the adequacy of federal warning labels.

The jury in the case decided that the tobacco company was negligent and made a dangerous and defective product in the case of Grady Carter, a Florida man who smoked for 50 years until he was diagnosed with cancer in 1991.
